en: National hero Jose Rizal was an ophthalmologist who used his medical skills to safely cure his mother’s cataracts, showing the importance of seeking eye doctors for vision problems.
Filipino scientist Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a cheap, safe bamboo incubator that uses hot water bottles to keep premature babies warm, teaching practical rural health sanitation.
The Department of Health endorses lagundi leaves as a safe, natural herbal medicine to effectively relieve coughs, promoting traditional plant-based health solutions for Filipino families.
Scientist Gregorio Zara invented a safer alcohol lamp, demonstrating how using controlled alcohol fuel prevents the dangerous house fires caused by spilled kerosene.
Under the Local Government Code, your local barangay maintains a disaster response team, teaching children to identify their nearest community evacuation center before typhoons.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan inspires neighbors to safely clear debris and share emergency food after typhoons, proving community cooperation saves lives during disasters.
Republic Act 10627, the Anti-Bullying Act, protects your right to a safe school environment, requiring students to immediately report bullying to their teachers.
The indigenous Ifugao people built the muyong woodlot system above rice terraces to safely absorb heavy rain and prevent deadly landslides.
The native Philippine calamansi fruit is packed with Vitamin C, which helps children build strong immune systems to safely fight off common colds.
Arnis, the Philippine national sport, teaches students practical self-defense and physical safety skills while improving their overall cardiovascular health and body coordination.
The Department of Health strictly enforces the No Smoking in Public Places law to protect children's developing lungs from dangerous secondhand smoke.
Scientist Dr. Ramon Barba discovered a safe potassium nitrate method to induce mango flowering without harsh chemicals, ensuring healthy, chemical-free fruits.
